purpose: Gabapentin enacarbil is used to treat Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), which causes uncomfortable sensations and an urge to move your legs, especially at night. It is also used to treat nerve pain that occurs after a shingles infection, called postherpetic neuralgia. It helps relieve discomfort so you can sleep better and feel more comfortable during the day.
how_it_works: This medication is a prodrug, meaning your body converts it into gabapentin after you swallow it. Gabapentin works by calming overactive nerve signals in your brain and nervous system that cause pain and that restless, crawling feeling in your legs. Think of it as turning down the volume on misfiring nerves so they stop sending uncomfortable messages.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dizziness, drowsiness or sleepiness, and headache. Some people also experience nausea, feeling unsteady or off-balance, and tiredness. These effects are often worse when you first start the medication or when your dose is increased.
warnings: This medication can make you very drowsy and dizzy, so do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication as it can dangerously increase drowsiness. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. There is also a small risk of mood changes or thoughts of self-harm, so contact your doctor right away if you feel depressed or have unusual thoughts.
typical_dosing: For Restless Legs Syndrome, the usual dose is 600 mg taken once daily with food in the evening, around 5 PM. For shingles nerve pain, the typical starting dose is 600 mg in the morning for 3 days, then increased to 600 mg twice daily. Always take it with food to help your body absorb it properly, and follow your doctor's specific instructions.
